relationships.subject: bradykinin
relationships.evidence_quote: Together, these results indicate that acute BK application can increase the intrinsic excitability of human sensory neurons.

relationships.subject: bradykinin
relationships.evidence_quote: Among repetitive-spiking neurons, prolonged exposure to BK led to an overall reduction in excitability (Figs. 5C–E), including a significant increase in rheobase and reduction in input resistance.

relationships.subject: human DRG nociceptors
relationships.evidence_quote: A majority (72.4%) of BDKRB2-expressing neurons also expressed SCN10A, indicating that BDKRB2-expressing cells are predominantly nociceptors (Fig. 2C).

relationships.subject: satellite glial cells
relationships.evidence_quote: Our results demonstrate that B2 receptors are also expressed on human satellite glial cells.

key_findings: Human DRG neurons express B2 (48-61%) and less B1 (<10%) receptors; acute bradykinin increases excitability while prolonged exposure reduces it in a subpopulation.
